_comment: Arc mainnet addresses. Every entry was verified on-chain with cast, not taken from a third party. Re-verify before mainnet deployment.

UniversalRouter.verified: execute(bytes,bytes[],uint256) 0x3593564c present; execute(bytes,bytes[]) 0x24856bc3 present; msgSender() 0xd737d0c7 present in bytecode and a live call returns address(0) WITHOUT reverting

Permit2.status: CONFIRMED - canonical address, same on every chain

V4Quoter.status: NOT YET VERIFIED - needs the official deployments page or an on-chain probe

evidence: 129 of the Initialize events sampled across blocks 29790463-29830463 have currency0 == address(0), i.e. real Arc v4 pools pair against NATIVE USDC
a sampled real pool had currency0=0x000..000, currency1=0xc816e521c38e92dc0408b4434f2c9bf0fecd6777, fee=2500, tickSpacing=50, hooks=address(0)
quoteCurrency.why: Pools must pair against native USDC to match the Arc ecosystem, so existing routers and indexers can see them. It is also strictly safer: currency.isAddressZero() cannot be spoofed, so the fake-USDC problem disappears entirely.

usdcErc20Interface.name: USDC
usdcErc20Interface.warning: SAME MONEY as native USDC but 1e12 apart. Never mix the two in accounting. WinCutHook pins exactly one via its immutable QUOTE and beforeInitialize rejects pools built on the other.

ecosystemConvention.note: WinCutLauncher uses fee 3000 / tickSpacing 60. Both are valid; fee and tickSpacing live in the PoolKey, not in the hook address, so changing them does NOT require re-mining the hook.

testnet.note: RPC is live and returns chain id 5042002, but a v4 deployment there is UNCONFIRMED. Develop against an Anvil fork of mainnet instead.
